newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids up on MGE recovery.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids up on MGE recovery.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat bids were slightly higher on Friday, in line with gains in MGE spring wheat futures, but movement remained slow as farmers waited for higher prices, cash grain dealers said.
"It's pretty quiet," a Montana dealer said. "A lot of people are getting anxious to sell but they're still not happy with the price."

One Minnesota dealer said movement was further slowed by a widely circulated report saying the IRS might impose a tax on certain deferred-payment grain contracts. While accountants downplayed the significance, farmers were concerned, he said.

"They want some of the money up front and now they've got the government saying they can't do deferred payment contracts tax-free," the dealer said. "The IRS, to a certain degree, is dictating grain movement this year."

Farmers have relied on the contracts for years as a means of deferring tax payments. Traditionally, they sell the grain at the end of the year and defer payment -- and tax bills -- until the following year.
But IRS ruled last December that a potato farmer in Washington state had to report income from a deferred-payment contract in the same year.
